name: Microhouse
about: Microhouse is house music shrunk to its smallest parts: clicks, pops and granular fragments in place of drum hits, bass reduced to a pulse, and vocals cut into syllables. It took shape between 1999 and 2002 in Cologne, Berlin, Frankfurt and Montreal, where producers on Kompakt, Perlon, Playhouse and Force Inc. crossed minimal techno's restraint with glitch's sound design and house's swing. Luomo's Vocalcity, Isolée's Rest, Jan Jelinek's Loop-Finding-Jazz-Records and Akufen's My Way are the founding records; Matthew Herbert and Ricardo Villalobos pushed it toward jazz and the fifteen-minute groove. The name faded after 2005, absorbed into the broader minimal scene, but its sound design is still audible in modern deep house and in half the records on Kompakt.

albums.title: Intershop
albums.why: Olaf Dettinger's Kompakt debut is the label's ambient-house cornerstone, soft loops and hiss that anticipated everything microhouse would do.

albums.title: Klick
albums.why: Brinkmann built these tracks from locked grooves cut into vinyl, and the result is minimal house as physical process, dry and hypnotic.

albums.title: Rest
albums.why: Rajko Müller's debut turned Beau Mot Plage's lilting guitar loop into an album of warped, humane house; the Playhouse label's finest hour.

albums.title: Vocalcity
albums.why: Vladislav Delay's house alias made six long tracks of dubbed-out, sighing vocal house, and the genre has been chasing its glow for twenty years.

albums.title: Loop-Finding-Jazz-Records
albums.why: Jazz LPs sampled down to crackle and grain and reassembled as swaying house; the most beautiful record in the clicks-and-cuts canon.

albums.title: Around the House
albums.why: Matthew Herbert's kitchen-sampled house album, with Dani Siciliano's vocals, is the earliest record that sounds fully like microhouse.

albums.title: Bodily Functions
albums.why: Sampled bodies and medical equipment under jazz-tinged songs; Herbert's masterpiece and the genre's most musically ambitious album.

albums.title: My Way
albums.why: Marc Leclair sampled slivers of FM radio into skipping house tracks, and Deck the House remains the signature microhouse single.

albums.title: Immer
albums.why: The Kompakt co-founder's mix defined the label's melancholy pop-minimal sound and is the best single introduction to the Cologne school.

albums.title: Textstar
albums.why: Jan Jelinek's house alias collects his Klang Elektronik singles, warm Rhodes fragments and shuffled clicks that still sound current.

albums.title: After Love
albums.why: Matias Aguayo and Dirk Leyers made Kompakt's most emotionally direct minimal record, with One Two Three (No Gravity) as its slow-burning hit.

albums.title: The Absence of Blight
albums.why: Peter Kersten's second album is the Dial sound in full: wistful, pastel minimal house with a melodic sense borrowed from pop.

albums.title: Alcachofa
albums.why: Easy Lee and Dexter stretched microhouse into something psychedelic and strange, and the album is the genre's most imitated and least matched.

albums.title: The Present Lover
albums.why: Luomo's follow-up to Vocalcity is more song-based and glossier, pop house with its edges filed down by dub.

albums.title: Here Comes Love
albums.why: Aksel Schaufler's debut is Kompakt as sad indie pop, half-sung and reverb-heavy, and Happiness is the standout.

albums.title: Thé au Harem d'Archimède
albums.why: Looser and more percussive than Alcachofa, built for Perlon, with the long-form grooves that made Villalobos the decade's definitive DJ.

albums.title: Diamond Daze
albums.why: Hendrik Weber's debut set bell tones and chimes over Dial's minimal house, and introduced the romantic strain the label became known for.

albums.title: We Are Monster
albums.why: Isolée's second album is wobblier and more playful than Rest, with Schrapnell and Pillowtalk showing how far microhouse could bend.

albums.title: Kosi Comes Around
albums.why: Koze's first solo album is Kompakt microhouse with a prankster's ear, loose grooves full of odd samples and sudden tenderness.

albums.title: Chromophobia
albums.why: The Brazilian producer's Kompakt debut is melodic minimal house at its most accessible, and Beautiful Life became the label's biggest crossover.

albums.title: This Bliss
albums.why: The second album refines the chime-and-bass formula into a complete sound world; Saturn Strobe and Asha are its peaks.

albums.title: From Here We Go Sublime
albums.why: Axel Willner's microscopic loops of pop records build into shoegaze house; Kompakt's biggest critical success and a genre landmark.

albums.title: Efdemin
albums.why: Phillip Sollmann's Dial debut is deep, swinging minimal house with a jazz pianist's harmony; Lohn & Brot is the keeper.

albums.title: Ay Ay Ay
albums.why: Aguayo built an album almost entirely from his own voice, a playful, Latin-tinged end point for the microhouse idea of the tiny sample.
